main_text.p: Restat ut me excusem de civilitate qua usus sum in te homi-Postea hæc edidit. Resp. ad Minervam Serrarii: Historiam sacr. Sulp. Severi cum comment. Opuscula Grammaticalia Grām. Ehr. Annot. seu præteritorum in N. T. libros decē. Librum de Henoch Comment. duplicem adnem maledicum. Nam hanc non nemo culpabit, scio: qui è dignitate mea fuisse censebit, siue malleum Grammaticorum, ferram Novatorum ita ut commeritus es, accepissem. Quod profecto fecissem si non mei rationem majorem habuissem. Non quid te, sed quid me decuit, spectavi. Vibanatim tetigi, alius rusticatim tanget. Non omnib. eadem conveniunt.

p.i: Responde stulto, inquit Sophus, secundum stultitiam ipsius

page.notes: The brace list is set as two columns; the lesson names are in italic. The first word of the imprint's last line is set in black letter-like initial form and read as "Stophorum" in the print; read here as Christophorum. Part of the page is cut off and not transcribed. Marginal notes on the right were partly cut at the edge; the Greek line and the final note are uncertain. The scan is cut off at the top and left, so the first lines may be incomplete.
